claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and any children you may have.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you're inquiring about for Child Benefit?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who is 4 years old. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Before I can assess your eligibility, I need to understand a bit more about your situation. Let me start by gathering some key details.

**First, does Alex live with you?** (In other words, is Alex in your care and living at your home?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex does live with me, but my ex-partner also lives with us and they already claim Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is important information. Let me make sure I understand the situation correctly:

**Can you confirm - your ex-partner is currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, and you all live together in the same household?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. We all live together in the same household, and my ex-partner is the one who claims the Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Before I can give you a final answer, I need to check the specific rules around this situation. Let me review the eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now provide you with a clear answer.

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules:

**Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child.** Since your ex-partner is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, you would not be eligible to also claim for the same child.

The rules state: "Two people cannot get Child Benefit for the same child. If you and someone else are responsible for the same child, agree between yourselves who will get Child Benefit."

In your situation, since Alex lives with you and your ex-partner in the same household, and your ex-partner is already receiving the benefit, only one of you can receive it - and that's currently your ex-partner.

If you wanted to change this arrangement, you and your ex-partner would need to agree to have the claim transferred to you instead. You could then contact HMRC to arrange this change.
